summary: Lewis and Clark NF lookout site in Teton County; the only dated record is a June 23, 1938 assignment naming a Bloody Hill lookout fireman. No status or site description found.

events.note: A June 23, 1938 assignment item from The Choteau Acantha, quoted on Forest Lookouts, names Al Gordon of Glacier Park as the Bloody Hill lookout fireman

evidence.supports: Bloody Hill is in Teton County on the Lewis and Clark National Forest, at 26N-10W-3 (township 26 north, range 10 west, section 3)
evidence.quote: Teton County - Lewis and Clark National Forest - 26N-10W-3

evidence.supports: the assignment item is dated June 23, 1938
the assignments run from Birch Creek south to and including the North Fork of the Sun River
evidence.quote: From Birch creek south to and including the north fork of the Sun river

evidence.supports: Al Gordon of Glacier Park is named as the Bloody Hill lookout fireman
evidence.quote: Al Gordon of Glacier Park, Bloody Hill lookout fireman.

evidence.supports: the item was printed in The Choteau Acantha
Bloody Hill is on the Teton County list of Forest Lookouts sites
the Teton County index lists Bloody Hill with four other lookouts: Beartop, Bennie Hill, Mount Wright and Wrong Ridge
evidence.quote: Beartop Bennie Hill Bloody Hill Mount Wright Wrong Ridge

notes_for_editor: Record fields (Teton County, Lewis and Clark NF, status unknown) match the Forest Lookouts pages; no correction proposed. The only dated item is the 1938 assignment quoted from a newspaper; the original was not read. Bloody Hill has no entry in the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Montana list, so the status stays unknown. One search result, a county summit-features listing, names a Bloody Hill in Teton County but was not read and is not cited. The 1938 assignment is the only evidence of a lookout here; no source describes the site now.
